question.text: The line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> is the directrix of the ellipse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> with the corresponding focus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. If the tangent to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> at the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> in the first quadrant passes through the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfenced></math> and intersects the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></mrow></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is equal to _____ .

solution.text:
Given,

The line x=8 is the directrix of the ellipse E:x2a2+y2b2=1 with the corresponding focus 2,0,

So, equation of directrix is given by x=ae⇒8=ae      …1

And distance of corresponding focus is given by,

ae=2          …2

So, from both equation we get,

8e=2e

⇒e2=14⇒e=12

Hence, a=4

Now using eccentricity formula we get,

b2=a21-e2=1634=12

Now equation of tangent to ellipse at point P4cosθ,12sinθ is given by,

xcosθ4+ysinθ23=1

Now given tangent passes through 0,43,

So, sinθ=12⇒θ=30°

Now, point P4cosθ,12sinθ will be P23,3

And intersection of tangent with x-axis will give Q83,0

Hence, by distance formula we get, 3PQ2=39
